name: Founder decision: Select and word the long-term commitments and the principles
text_content:
The record holds candidates for both and has never sorted them.

Long-term commitment candidates: the three compounding engines (organization, customer, brand); the leading indicators the white paper commits to (employee NPS, cultural labor score, customer recognition rate); a company "built to run without them" (WP p. 06); coherence across the day, each service period with its own reason to exist. None carries a figure, which is what makes them well formed.

Principle candidates, stated in the record as mechanics: authority lives in the domain; the first question is what allowed this, not who failed; management absorbs blame from staff; if it matters to the experience, Sŏn pays for it; there is no hierarchy of importance; never assert the unproven; advancement requires preparation, not permission; employees are the users.

Brandon selects which are long-term commitments, which are principles, and which are operating rules belonging to Session 3, then words each under canon's voice rules.

Two constraints Session 2 recommends: version one is marked pre-opening and drawn from decisions rather than moments, because Sŏn has decisions and no operating history; and every principle passes canon's six binary tests, which rules out the virtue register Stripe uses and forces the statement of what the company does or refuses.

Filed by Session 2. Reasoning is in sections 6.2, 6.3, and 6.4 of the S2 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.
